title: How to Ask Your Counselor the Right Questions This…
summary: IB students: ask your counselor the right questions this fall about deadlines, predicted grades, references, transcripts, and university choices.
body_markdown:
For an IB student applying to university, the best counselor meeting produces decisions, deadlines, and clear next steps. To **ask your counselor the right questions this fall** , concentrate on information only your school can confirm: internal deadlines, predicted-grade procedures, references, transcripts, application platforms, and responsibility for each document.


The September-November period is especially important because many early US deadlines and the UCAS deadline for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry, and veterinary courses fall within it. Preparing specific questions helps you leave the meeting with a workable application plan rather than general advice.


### Understand your counselor's role


University counselors commonly help students interpret admissions requirements, build balanced university lists, manage school documents, and follow application procedures. Responsibilities vary, however. Subject teachers, the **DP coordinator** , administrative staff, and the counselor may handle different parts of the same application.


Ask: **“Which parts are handled by you, my teachers, the DP coordinator, and me?”** Your counselor might submit a school transcript, while the DP coordinator later authorizes the IB to send final results.


Counselors cannot guarantee admission, independently change a teacher's prediction, or override published entry requirements. Their role is to explain the process, identify problems, and help the school provide accurate information.


### Bring a one-page application brief


Give your counselor a concise document containing:


- Your intended degree subject or possible academic areas
- Your six IB subjects, identified as **HL** or **SL**
- Current and predicted grades, if your school shares them
- Countries and application systems under consideration
- A preliminary university list
- Official and school-imposed deadlines
- Required tests, interviews, portfolios, or financial-aid forms
- Two or three questions requiring a decision


The[RevisionDojo global IB university application guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-apply-to-university-as-an-ib-student-step-by-step-guide-for-global-admissions) can help you organize this information. The brief does not need to present a finished plan. It should give your counselor enough detail to offer specific advice.


### Ask about internal deadlines first


Your first deadline question should be: **“What are our school's internal deadlines for each document?”** Schools need time to check applications, prepare transcripts, collect recommendations, approve predictions, and complete references. The internal deadline can therefore be substantially earlier than the university deadline.


For **2027 UK entry** , UCAS states that Oxford, Cambridge, and most medicine, dentistry, and veterinary medicine or science applications must arrive by **15 October 2026 at 18:00 UK time** . The equal-consideration deadline for most other undergraduate courses is **13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time** . A school linked to your UCAS application may require submission earlier so that it can add the reference and review the application.


US deadlines vary by institution and admission plan. Ask which dates apply to your exact colleges and when school documents must be requested, then verify each date on the institution's official admissions website.


### Ask how predicted grades are produced


For many IB applicants, predicted grades are a significant school-provided part of the application. Ask:


- **When are application predictions finalized?**
- **Which assessments contribute to them?**
- **Does the school disclose predictions to students?**
- **Can later evidence be considered before submission?**
- **Who approves and sends them?**
- **Are application forecasts the same as predictions later submitted to the IB?**


A predicted grade is an evidence-based school judgment, not a target selected by the student or an achieved result. Procedures differ between schools, so another student's experience may not apply to you.


If a prediction is below a course requirement, ask what evidence supports it and which remaining assessment could demonstrate the next grade level. The[guide to predicted grades and university offers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/predicted-grades-and-university-offers) explains why total points, HL grades, and subject prerequisites must be considered separately.


### Test whether your university list is balanced


Ask your counselor: **“Which choices are ambitious, realistic, and safer based on my current evidence?”** Meeting a published minimum does not guarantee admission, particularly for selective courses.


Question to verify Why it matters


What total IB score is expected? It indicates whether your overall prediction is competitive.


Are specific HL subjects required? A high total cannot replace a missing prerequisite.


Are minimum HL grades specified? Offers may include a total and an HL combination.


Is a test, interview, or portfolio required? These can have separate registration deadlines.


Is financial aid available? Academic suitability and affordability must be assessed together.


Ask whether your subject combination creates an eligibility problem. Students sometimes concentrate on total points while overlooking a required Mathematics, science, or language course at HL.


### Clarify transcripts, references, and final results


Ask: **“Which academic record will the school send, and what will it contain?”** A school transcript may include several years of internal grades, while predicted IB grades may appear separately. The final **IB transcript of grades** is a different document issued by the IB after results are released.


For US applications, Common App identifies the **School Report** as a core counselor form that typically accompanies the school profile and transcript. Colleges separately determine whether they require a counselor recommendation, Midyear Report, or additional forms. The[RevisionDojo guide to reporting the IB in US applications](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-in-college-apps-us) explains these distinctions.


If a recommendation is required, provide a concise brag sheet with accomplishments, interests, responsibilities, goals, and examples of academic growth or contribution. Ask whether midyear grades will be sent and who monitors that requirement.


Also ask how final IB results will reach the university you attend. The IB states that current-session students arrange pre-results transcript requests through their coordinator or university and career counselor. Eligible requests made before results are released can send results to up to **six higher education institutions** without charge, and UCAS counts as one request. Later requests may involve a fee.


### Discuss circumstances requiring context


Your counselor may explain illness, family responsibilities, disrupted schooling, timetable conflicts, or limited subject availability. Ask: **“Could admissions readers misunderstand any part of my record without school context?”**


Share only the information needed and discuss how it will be communicated. Context should help the university interpret your record accurately, not attempt to excuse every weak result. Counselors can also explain the school's curriculum, grading system, class-rank policy, and available IB subjects.


### End with an action record


Finish by asking: **“Can we confirm the next action, the responsible person, and the due date?”** Record the answer immediately.


Action Owner Due date


Confirm course prerequisites Student 25 September


Finalize predicted grades Subject teachers School deadline


Submit counselor questionnaire Student 1 October


Upload school report Counselor Internal deadline


Send a brief follow-up email restating important decisions. This creates a shared record and reduces the need for repeated progress enquiries.


### Common mistakes to avoid


Avoid asking only, “Where should I apply?” Counselors give stronger advice when they can compare your interests, academic evidence, constraints, and researched options.


Other common mistakes include:


- Treating a minimum score as an admissions guarantee
- Ignoring internal deadlines because the platform closes later
- Confusing school transcripts, predictions, and final IB transcripts
- Requesting a higher prediction without new academic evidence
- Assuming one country's process applies everywhere
- Leaving document requests until the final week


If predictions remain a concern, turn the discussion into a measurable academic plan. The[guide to early-application predicted grades](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-do-ib-predicted-grades-work-for-early-university-applications-a-complete-guide) and[RevisionDojo guidance for university counselors](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-for-university-counselors) explain how targeted practice and timed evidence can support informed conversations. Official predictions remain the school's responsibility.


### Conclusion


To ask your counselor the right questions this fall, focus on responsibilities, internal deadlines, predictions, course requirements, references, transcripts, and later documents. Bring a researched list and leave with every action assigned to a person and date.


You remain responsible for checking requirements and completing student sections accurately. RevisionDojo can support the academic part of your plan through Study Notes, the Questionbank, Mock Exams, and Jojo AI when your counselor identifies a subject weakness or required grade.
